chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Sunday morning concerts after Saturday nights at Bricktop's
summary: They played unpaid weekly concerts at 9 a.m. on Sundays for young listeners, after working at Bricktop's until dawn.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, you were doing a series of concerts, monthly concerts, or --

Well, weekly concerts, at the little Concert Hall, I don't remember the name of it now, on Square Lafayette, not far from the Hotel Lafayette, somewhere around there on the way to the North Station, Gare du Nord.
They would charge admission, every Sunday morning. Now, just imagine how good we were. We were working at Chez Bricktop's every Saturday night, everybody goes there.
Around about 4:00, 4:30, and at 9:00 we were in a concert hall playing. 9:00 on Sunday morning.
And for nothing. So we just --
Well, this was what, students that would come in mostly, mostly young people?

Yes, young people, yes. And a certain variety of students with their parents; very nice people. Select. More or less select 'cause you -- in the first place you have to have a certain situation to be able to pay, pay for the
Well, we did that for years and years it continued until we went to the Salle de Pleyel -- did I speak of the Salle de Pleyel?
Well, that was after Canetti got into it.
